subject: Private observability collector topology & snooping mitigation

Subject: Private observability collector topology & snooping mitigation

Hi all,

Attaching an updated sketch (collector-topology-v2.png) of the visibility topology for AcmeCorp's private VPC deployment. High level: a single-tenant collector cluster inside the customer's enclave that forwards scrubbed telemetry to their SIEM over an egress proxy; a lightweight sidecar handles trace hooks and sample keys.

Ask: can we confirm whether the proposed design meets Acme's internal snooping expectations? Specifically:
- Where should we terminate TLS for instrumentation (collector vs egress proxy)?
- Do you require per-service client certificates or will a single collector cert suffice?
- Are there any onboarding checks SecOps requires before we accept telemetry from an enclave (e.g., signed manifest, key attestation)?

I've also attached a short mitigation checklist (snooping-mitigation-checklist.md) with options 1-3 so we can align on the least invasive path.

Proposed next step: quick alignment call tomorrow; I can share the design and we can mark JIRA-SUP-4578 with decisions.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@aurasys.net>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 13:47:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Private observability collector topology & snooping mitigation

Thanks Mina — this looks useful. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Termination: Acme prefers TLS termination at our egress proxy to keep all raw telemetry inside the enclave until it reaches a hardened boundary. So collector->egress should be mTLS with an internal cert, then egress->SIEM using an outbound corporate cert.

2) Per-service certs: Ideally we don't want many certs to manage. A single collector cert is acceptable if the collector can present per-service metadata (service name, env) and we have attestable manifest signing to tie payloads to an approved binary.

3) Onboarding checks: SecOps will require a signed manifest and a short attestation that the collector binary is the exact hash approved in SUP-4578. They also asked for a list of what fields we will scrub before egress (PII, user-id, request body).

I can be on the call tomorrow; secops@acmecorp.com will route specific policy questions to their internal lead.

- Carlos
Carlos Ruiz
Principal Architect, Aurasys (Acme integration)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@aurasys.net>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability collector topology & snooping mitigation

Thanks Carlos — that's helpful and aligns with what we recommend. A couple of operational notes and mitigations we propose: 

- Termination at egress proxy: agree. We'll make the collector->egress link mTLS and add an option for an internal HMACed manifest header (x-obs-manifest-signature) so Acme can verify provenance without seeing full binaries.

- Single collector cert: ok. To reduce blast radius, we will support short-lived device cert rotation (7–30 day TTL) with automated renewal via the customer's KMS. That keeps operational overhead low while meeting least-privilege goals.

- Scrubbing: propose a default scrub profile that strips request bodies > 256 bytes, hashes email-like tokens, and removes fields labeled in our mapping as PII. We'll share the scrub profile JSON on the call.

- Telemetry sampling & traces: for trace hooks we will only export sampled spans that include a minimal service identifier and no user identifiers. We will add an explicit flag in the agent to drop tag keys that match regexes provided by Acme.

I've added all action items to JIRA-SUP-4578 and uploaded the scrub profile in the Drive link (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-collector-design).

On the call: let's finalize the manifest format and the cert rotation cadence. Who from Acme SecOps will own the final attestation check?

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
